proposal.reactor_type: Heated stainless-steel/PFA coil reactor (liquid-liquid homogeneous Suzuki coupling), oil-bath or aluminum block heating
proposal.tubing_material: PFA (or 316 SS if Pd sticking/fouling is a concern)
proposal.residence_time_basis: Liquid-phase, single-phase homogeneous flow; residence time = reactor volume / total combined flow rate (no gas expansion correction needed)

streams.contents: Aromatic bromide (1.0 equiv) + Pd catalyst (e.g., Pd(PPh3)4 or Pd(OAc)2/ligand, 3 mol%)
Phenylboronic acid derivative (1.2 equiv) + K2CO3 base (2.5 equiv)

proposal.mixer_type: PEEK/stainless steel T-mixer or low-volume static mixer (<50 µL) upstream of heated coil
proposal.mixing_order_reasoning: ArBr/Pd stream and boronic acid/base stream are combined immediately before the heated zone to avoid premature Pd-mediated protodeboronation or catalyst decomposition at elevated temperature prior to oxidative addition; rapid T-mixing ensures homogeneous stoichiometry entering the reactor.
pre_reactor_steps: Degas both DMF stock solutions with N2 sparge to prevent Pd(0) oxidation
0.2 µm inline filtration of boronic acid/base stream to remove undissolved carbonate particulates and prevent clogging
Preheat both streams to ~40 C in a preheat loop before mixing to minimize thermal gradient shock at the T-mixer
post_reactor_steps: In-line back-pressure regulator (8 bar) to suppress CO2 microbubble formation from carbonate base and maintain single-phase flow at 50 C
Post-reactor cooling loop (ambient water bath) to quench reaction before BPR
Optional inline aqueous workup (liquid-liquid separator) to remove residual Pd/base salts
proposal.chemistry_notes: This is a standard Suzuki-Miyaura cross-coupling. Microwave batch conditions (50 W, 50 C, 10 min) are dielectric-heating equivalent to conductive/convective heating in a coil reactor at the same bulk temperature; residence time is matched 1:1 assuming no strong non-thermal MW effect (well-documented for Pd-catalyzed couplings, which are considered thermal in nature). DMF is used as a fully miscible co-solvent with water to solubilize inorganic base without phase separation in narrow tubing.

reasoning_per_field.residence_time_min: Matched directly to batch microwave irradiation time (10 min), assuming coupling kinetics are thermally controlled rather than MW-specific.
reasoning_per_field.flow_rate_mL_min: Derived from reactor_volume_mL (5.0) / residence_time_min (10) = 0.5 mL/min total; split evenly across two 0.25 mL/min streams for 1:1 volumetric mixing.
reasoning_per_field.temperature_C: Matches reported batch bulk temperature (50 C); microwave power (50 W) is treated as the heating method to reach this bulk temperature, not an independent reaction parameter.
reasoning_per_field.concentration_M: Assumed batch reaction volume of ~4 mL for 1.6 mmol ArBr (typical microwave vial fill volume), giving 0.4 M; not explicitly stated in protocol, so treated as an assumption.
reasoning_per_field.BPR_bar: 8 bar chosen to suppress CO2 outgassing from carbonate base reacting with boronic acid/protons and to keep DMF/H2O mixture single-phase at 50 C; well below DMF bp (153 C) so pressure need is modest.
reasoning_per_field.reactor_volume_mL: Set to 5.0 mL to satisfy residence_time_min = reactor_volume/flow_rate at a practical, commercially available coil size.
reasoning_per_field.tubing_ID_mm: 1.0 mm ID balances reasonable flow rates with laminar mixing and low fouling risk from inorganic base/Pd catalyst.
reasoning_per_field.mixer_type: T-mixer selected for simplicity and low dead volume; adequate for two miscible liquid streams without need for advanced multilamination.
reasoning_per_field.BPR_bar_alt_consideration: Could be lowered to 3-5 bar if no CO2-generating base is used, but 8 bar chosen conservatively for K2CO3 system.

literature_analogies: Suzuki-Miyaura couplings in continuous flow using PFA/glass microreactors (Noel, Buchwald, Jensen groups) reproducing microwave batch condition with matched residence time and comparable yields (85-95%).

Organic Process Research & Development reports on translating MW-assisted Pd-catalyzed cross-couplings into coil-flow reactors at equivalent bulk temperatures, confirming thermal (non-specific MW) origin of rate acceleration.
safety_flags: DMF is a reproductive toxicant (Cat 1B) and moderate inhalation hazard - use closed system with fume extraction at pump/reservoir access points
Pd catalyst handling - use glovebox or Schlenk techniques for stock solution prep to prevent air/moisture-induced decomposition
CO2 gas evolution from base neutralization - ensure BPR and vented collection vessel to avoid pressure buildup
Boronic acid derivatives may be moisture sensitive; verify solubility/stability in aqueous DMF over the intended residence time
System pressure (8 bar) requires rated fittings and pressure relief valve upstream of BPR
